docs.title: What Is Upscale SDK?
docs.text: UpscaleSDK is a Unity SDK that abstracts platform-specific features required to ship console and desktop games, including input handling, save data, social features, UI navigation, and build validation.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
• Desktop - Windows, macOS, Linux
  • Xbox - Series X/S, One
  • PlayStation - PS4, PS5
  • Nintendo Switch

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. Getting Started - install the SDK and bootstrap it in a scene
  2. Manual → Core - one page per Core subsystem
  3. Manual → Platform - per-platform setup checklists
  4. API Reference - generated from the source tree

See also: Unity Compatibility · Roadmap

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: A snapshot of what is shipped, in progress, and planned.

docs.title: Shipped
docs.text:
• Core runtime - Saves, Input and UI modules
  • Major console and desktop platforms
  • Build validation
  • Base console social functions (Achievements, Activities)
  • Sample scenes - Input, Saves, UI

docs.title: In progress
docs.text: Nothing currently in development. Focusing on stabilization and architectural planning.

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• Keyboard/mouse support for input
  • Better saves
  • Improve API/remove API placeholders
  • Select gamepad mappings for in editor testing
  • Localization module

docs.title: Under consideration
docs.text:
• Multilingual Documentation
  • Refactoring/architectural cleanups
  • Improve input builder API
  • More gamepad functions (lightbar)

Tip

Have a request? Open an issue on the GitHub repository and tag it roadmap.

Valid characters for the file name portion (everything after the final forward slash) include uppercase letters (A-Z), lowercase letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), underscore (), period (.), and hyphen (-). docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Follow this setup guide once for every new Unity project. All other documentation assumes these steps are already completed.

docs.title: 1. Install Unity dependencies
docs.text:
The SDK needs Newtonsoft.Json for save serialisation. Install it via Window → Package Manager → + → Add package by name:

  • com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json

For console-specific package and middleware requirements, see each platform's setup page - they vary per target.

docs.title: 2. Import the Core package
docs.text:
Import UpscaleSDK-Core.unitypackage from your distribution into the project. It contains:

  • Assets/UpscaleSDK/BootstrapScene - the runtime bootstrap scene
  • Assets/UpscaleSDK/Core - all cross-platform modules (Input, Saves, UI, Configuration, Utils, Validator)
  • Assets/UpscaleSDK/Platform/Desktop - the Desktop platform layer

docs.title: 3. Import the platform packages you ship on
docs.text:
Import the per-platform .unitypackages for every target you build. Each platform page lists the extra packages, assembly definition references, and middleware its layer needs:

  • Desktop - already included in Core, no extra import needed
  • Xbox - UpscaleSDK-Xbox.unitypackage
  • PlayStation 4 - UpscaleSDK-PS4.unitypackage
  • PlayStation 5 - UpscaleSDK-PS5.unitypackage
  • Nintendo Switch - UpscaleSDK-Switch.unitypackage

docs.title: 4. (Optional) Import samples and extras
docs.text:
• UpscaleSDK-Samples.unitypackage - runnable example scenes for Input, Saves, and UI (see Samples)
  • UpscaleSDK-Extras.unitypackage - optional content under Assets/UpscaleSDK/Extras

docs.title: 5. Add the Bootstrap scene
docs.text: Open Assets/UpscaleSDK/BootstrapScene and add it as the first entry in Build Settings → Scenes In Build.

docs.title: 6. Configure the SDK
docs.text:
Create or locate the UpscaleSDKConfig asset at Resources/UpscaleSDK, name it Config and fill in the fields you need:

  • Saves Settings - autosave interval, file extension, container / save size per platform (see Manual → Saves → Setup)
  • GamepadIconsSet references - per platform glyph sets used by the Input module (see Manual → Input → Glyphs)

docs.title: 7. Verify with the Validator
docs.text: Run Tools → UpscaleSDK → Validate Project and resolve any reported issues before building.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Input - action-based gamepad input
  • Saves - cross-platform key/value persistence
  • UI - controller-friendly menu navigation
  • Validator - build-time project checks

docs.title: Input
docs.text: The Input module provides a strongly-typed, action-based abstraction over Unity new input system that works the same way on Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch. You describe what the player wants to do (Jump, Move, Apply) and the SDK maps it to the appropriate device button or axis at runtime.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Action-based input - bind, read by name or reference
  • Strongly-typed actions - bool, float, Vector2
  • Binding builder - chain BindAs… → To… → WithProcessor… → Complete()
  • Pre-made action set (BaseInputActionSet) for common usage
  • Custom action sets - group your game-specific actions
  • Cross-platform action mapping - Apply / Cancel resolve to the right face button per platform
  • Pluggable processors - deadzone, invert, repeat-delay, or your own IProcessor<T>
  • Controller glyph support - per-platform icon sets
  • Provider abstraction - the runtime decouples your code from Unity new Input System
  • Event-based or polled - subscribe to Performed, or call .Read()

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Input System is automatically initialized by the RuntimeBootstrap component during application startup. It is also automatically deinitialized when the OnDestroy lifecycle event is triggered, allowing the system to correctly release resources and unregister callbacks.

Warning

You must have an UpscaleSDKConfig asset at Resources/UpscaleSDK/Config with glyph sets assigned for every platform you plan to ship on. Without it, TryGetGlyph() returns null and gamepad detection on Desktop platform falls back to GamepadType.None.

docs.title: Subscribe to input events
docs.text:
private void OnEnable()
{
    BaseInputActionSet.Instance.Apply.Press.Performed += OnApply;
}

private void OnDisable()
{
    BaseInputActionSet.Instance.Apply.Press.Performed -= OnApply;
}

private void OnApply(bool pressed)
{
    Debug.Log($"Apply pressed: {pressed}");
}

Always unsubscribe in OnDisable / OnDestroy - InputAction<T> events are long-lived and will keep your objects alive otherwise.

docs.title: Action, Action Group, Action Set, Action Definition
docs.text: Term What it is InputAction<T> A single named input that produces a value of type T and fires Performed ButtonActionGroup A button bundled (based on InputAction<T>) into its three trigger variants: Press, Hold, Release InputActionsSet<T> A collection of actions you activate/deactivate as a single unit InputActionDefinition<T> A ScriptableObject asset that authors an action in the Inspector

docs.title: Button triggers
docs.text:
Every button can exposed as three actions via ButtonActionGroup:

Trigger Fires Press Once on the frame the button goes down Hold Every frame while the button is held Release Once on the frame the button goes up 
BaseInputActionSet.Instance.South.Press.Performed   += OnJumpStart;
BaseInputActionSet.Instance.South.Hold.Performed    += OnJumpCharging;
BaseInputActionSet.Instance.South.Release.Performed += OnJumpRelease;

docs.title: Cross-platform action mapping
docs.text:
Some semantic actions (Apply, Cancel, …) automatically resolve to the right physical button on each platform. Use these instead of hard-coding South / East when you want platform-appropriate button mappings.

Action PS 4 PS 5 Switch Xbox Apply X / O X A A Cancel O / X O B B Base Square Square X Y Extra Triangle Triangle Y X 
BaseInputActionSet.Instance.Apply.Press.Performed  += OnConfirm;
BaseInputActionSet.Instance.Cancel.Press.Performed += OnBack;

docs.title: BaseInputActionSet
docs.text:
BaseInputActionSet is the pre-made set covering every standard gamepad input. It is created lazily on first access to .Instance.

Category Members Face buttons (raw) South, West, North, East Face buttons (mapped) Apply, Cancel, Base, Extra System buttons Start, Select Shoulders / stick clicks LeftShoulder, RightShoulder, LeftStickButton, RightStickButton D-pad buttons DpadUp, DpadDown, DpadLeft, DpadRight Triggers (float) LeftTrigger, RightTrigger Stick axes (float) LeftStickX, LeftStickY, RightStickX, RightStickY Sticks / D-pad (Vector2) LeftStick, RightStick, DPad

All button members are ButtonActionGroup (.Press / .Hold / .Release). Float and Vector2 members are InputAction<float> / InputAction<Vector2>.

docs.title: Custom action sets
docs.text:
For game-specific input, subclass InputActionsSet<T> and define your bindings in Initialize:

public sealed class PlayerInputActionSet : InputActionsSet<PlayerInputActionSet>
{
    public InputAction<bool>    Interact { get; private set; }
    public InputAction<Vector2> Move     { get; private set; }
    public InputAction<float>   Aim      { get; private set; }

    protected override void Initialize(InputSetBuilder builder)
    {
        Interact = builder.BindAsBool("Interact")
                          .ToAction(GamepadAction.Apply, ButtonTrigger.Press)
                          .Complete();

        Move     = builder.BindAsVector2("Move")
                          .ToLeftStick()
                          .WithDeadzone(0.15f)
                          .Complete();

        Aim      = builder.BindAsFloat("Aim")
                          .ToRightTrigger()
                          .Complete();
    }
}

Access through the singleton:

PlayerInputActionSet.Instance.Move.Performed += OnMove;

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
// Enable/disable callbacks for the entire set
PlayerInputActionSet.Instance.Activate();
PlayerInputActionSet.Instance.Deactivate();

bool isActive = PlayerInputActionSet.Instance.IsActive;

// Release all bindings registered by this set
PlayerInputActionSet.Instance.Dispose();

Deactivate() is the right tool for "pause player input while a menu is open." Dispose() is the right tool for scene unload or shutdown.

docs.title: Action Definitions
docs.text:
InputActionDefinition is the asset-based counterpart to the fluent builder. Each definition is a ScriptableObject that holds a list of input sources and a list of processors; at runtime, calling .Build() returns a wired-up InputAction<T>. Use them when you want input to be authored in the Inspector - by designers, modders, or just so the binding lives next to the prefab that consumes it - instead of expressed in code.

Definition asset Value type Returns BoolActionDefinition bool InputAction<bool> FloatActionDefinition float InputAction<float> Vector2ActionDefinition Vector2 InputAction<Vector2>

docs.title: Creating a definition
docs.text: Project window → right-click → Create → Upscale SDK → Input → Actions → <Bool / Float / Vector2> Action

docs.title: Configuring it
docs.text:
In the inspector you fill two reorderable lists:

  • Sources - one or more IInputSource<T> instances (e.g. a gamepad button source, a stick axis source). The dropdown is auto-populated with every concrete IInputSource<T> matching the asset's value type.
  • Processors - one or more IProcessor<T> instances applied in order. The custom editor warns if you add the same processor type twice.

Both lists use [SerializeReference] so custom subclasses you write in your own assembly appear in the dropdowns automatically - no editor code required.

docs.title: Building at runtime
docs.text:
[SerializeField] private BoolActionDefinition _interactDefinition;
[SerializeField] private Vector2ActionDefinition _moveDefinition;

private InputAction<bool>    _interact;
private InputAction<Vector2> _move;

private void OnEnable()
{
    _interact = _interactDefinition.Build();
    _move     = _moveDefinition.Build();

    _interact.Performed += OnInteract;
    _move.Performed     += OnMove;
}

private void OnDisable()
{
    _interact.Performed -= OnInteract;
    _move.Performed     -= OnMove;

    _interact.Dispose();
    _move.Dispose();
}

Each .Build() call registers a new binding under a freshly generated GUID, so the same asset can be built multiple times (e.g. one per player) without collisions. The returned InputAction<T> is the same type you'd get from UPSInput.BindAs<T>(...).Complete() - .Read(), .Performed, and .TryGetGlyph() all work identically.

Tip

Definitions and custom action sets are not mutually exclusive - a custom InputActionsSet<T> can serialise [SerializeField] InputActionDefinition<T> fields and call .Build() on them inside Initialize(...), which gives you a set that's partly code-defined and partly asset-defined.

docs.title: Static API (UPSInput)
docs.text:
Use the static API when an action does not belong to a long-lived set - for example one-off bindings, editor tools, or runtime-defined inputs.

// Bind
UPSInput.BindAsBool("Interact")
        .ToButton(GamepadButton.ButtonSouth, ButtonTrigger.Press)
        .Complete();

// Subscribe / unsubscribe
UPSInput.Subscribe<bool>("Interact", OnInteract);
UPSInput.Unsubscribe<bool>("Interact", OnInteract);

// Toggle an individual action
UPSInput.SetActionState("Interact", active: false);

// Remove a binding entirely
UPSInput.Unbind("Interact");

docs.title: Device queries
docs.text:
GamepadType pad         = UPSInput.GetGamepadType();          // None / Nintendo / PlayStation / Xbox
DeviceType[] connected  = UPSInput.GetConnectedDevices();     // Keyboard, Gamepad

docs.title: Binding builder
docs.text:
Danger

This API is gamepad-only today. Mouse and keyboard support is on the Roadmap, and the binding entry points (To…, With…) will likely gain new overloads or be renamed when those sources land.

Every binding follows the same shape - three required calls, with optional processors in between:

BindAs...(name)  →  To...(…)  →  WithProcessor(processor)  →  Complete()

docs.title: Bool
docs.text:
Source Method A physical button .ToButton(GamepadButton, ButtonTrigger) A semantic action .ToAction(GamepadAction, ButtonTrigger) Inversion .WithInvert() 
UPSInput.BindAsBool("Jump")
        .ToButton(GamepadButton.ButtonSouth, ButtonTrigger.Press)
        .Complete();

docs.title: Float
docs.text:
Source Method Left stick X / Y .ToXLeftStick() / .ToYLeftStick() Right stick X / Y .ToXRightStick() / .ToYRightStick() Triggers .ToLeftTrigger() / .ToRightTrigger() Inversion .WithInvert() 
UPSInput.BindAsFloat("Aim").ToRightTrigger().Complete();

docs.title: Vector2
docs.text:
Source Method Sticks .ToLeftStick() / .ToRightStick() D-pad .ToDpad() Deadzone .WithDeadzone(float) Axis inversion .WithInvertX() / .WithInvertY() 
UPSInput.BindAsVector2("Move")
        .ToLeftStick()
        .WithDeadzone(0.15f)
        .WithInvertY()
        .Complete();

docs.title: Processors
docs.text: Processors transform input values between the source and the consumer. They implement IProcessor<T> and are attached with .WithProcessor(...).

docs.title: Built-in processors
docs.text: Processor T Behaviour InvertBoolProcessor bool Returns !value InvertFloatProcessor float Returns -value InvertXVector2Processor Vector2 Negates X, preserves Y InvertYVector2Processor Vector2 Preserves X, negates Y DeadzoneVector2Processor Vector2 Returns Vector2.zero if magnitude is below the deadzone threshold DelayVector2Processor Vector2 Normalises to cardinal axes and repeats with initialDelay / repeatDelay - designed for D-pad/Stick

docs.title: Custom processors
docs.text:
Any class implementing IProcessor<T> can be plugged in:

[Serializable]
public sealed class ScaleVector2Processor : IProcessor<Vector2>
{
    [SerializeField] private float _factor;

    public ScaleVector2Processor(float factor) => _factor = factor;

    public Vector2 Process(Vector2 value) => value * _factor;

    public IProcessor<Vector2> Clone() => (IProcessor<Vector2>)MemberwiseClone();
}

Clone() is called when the same processor instance is shared across multiple bindings and one of them needs an isolated copy of the internal state - implement it via MemberwiseClone() unless you hold reference-type state.

Usage:

builder.BindAsVector2("Move")
       .ToLeftStick()
       .WithProcessor(new ScaleVector2Processor(1.5f))
       .Complete();

Processors can be chained - each is applied in registration order.

docs.title: Glyphs
docs.text:
TryGetGlyph() returns the controller-specific sprite for an action, so you can show the right icon in tooltips and prompts.

Sprite icon = BaseInputActionSet.Instance.Apply.Press.TryGetGlyph();
// or via the static API
Sprite east = UPSInput.TryGetGlyph(GamepadGlyph.East);

docs.title: Authoring icon sets
docs.text:
You need one GamepadIconsSet per platform you ship on.

1. Create the icon sets

Project window → right-click → Create → Upscale SDK → Gamepad Icons Set

Name them descriptively, e.g. PlayStation5_Icons, Xbox_Icons, Switch_Icons.

2. Assign sprites

Open each set in the Inspector and drop a sprite into every GamepadGlyph slot (face buttons, D-pad, sticks, shoulders, triggers, Start / Select).

3. Wire the sets into UpscaleSDKConfig

Open your UpscaleSDKConfig asset and assign each platform's GamepadIconsSet to the matching field. GlyphProvider will pick the correct set at runtime based on UPSInput.GetGamepadType().

Tip

The optional UpscaleSDK-Extras.unitypackage already includes pre-configured GamepadIconsSet assets for PlayStation / Xbox / Switch.

docs.title: Saves
docs.text: The Saves module is a platform-agnostic save system that gives you a Unity PlayerPrefs style key/value API on every platform - Desktop, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch without the per-platform plumbing leaking into your game code.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Key/value API - Get/Set for int, float, string, bool
  • One API everywhere - same calls on Desktop, Xbox, PS4 / PS5, Switch
  • Auto-save timer - periodic flush to disk, interval is configurable
  • JSON serialisation - human-readable files via Newtonsoft.Json, polymorphism supported (TypeNameHandling.All)

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
The save system is initialised automatically by RuntimeBootstrap once the active Platform is ready.

What you need to do:

  1. An UpscaleSDKConfig asset, named as Config at Resources/UpscaleSDK/.
  2. A SavesSettings reference assigned on that config (see Configuration).

Warning

Before using the save system, ensure that the platform-specific initialization has completed. The recommended setup is to use the UPSBootstrap scene as the first scene in Build Settings.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
The recommended way to start using the save system is through UPSSaves.Prefs, this is primary high-level API for reading and writing save data and should cover most common use cases.

public sealed class ScoreBoard : MonoBehaviour
{
    private void Load()
    {
        int score    = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetInt("score", 0);
        string name  = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetString("playerName", "Unknown");
        bool tutorial = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetBool("tutorialSeen", false);
    }

    public void RecordWin(int newScore)
    {
        UPSSaves.Prefs.SetInt("score", newScore);
        UPSSaves.Prefs.SetBool("tutorialSeen", true);
        UPSSaves.Prefs.TrySave();   // explicit flush (auto-save fires on its own timer too)
    }
}

TrySave() is a no-op if the system isn't ready, so it is safe to call at any time.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Term What it is UPSSaves Facade, exposes Prefs and Saver and signals IsReady UPSPlayerPrefs The everyday key/value API (drop-in mental model: Unity's PlayerPrefs) Saver Lower-level system - owns the in-memory Dictionary<string,string>, drives I/O, UPSPlayerPrefs uses this for save/load logic AutoSaver Interval timer that calls TrySave() automatically SavesSettings ScriptableObject of configuration: autosave interval, file extension, container name

docs.title: UPSPlayerPrefs - key/value saves
docs.text: This is what most game code talks to. Access via UPSSaves.Prefs.

docs.title: Get / Set
docs.text:
UPSSaves.Prefs.SetInt("level", 7);
UPSSaves.Prefs.SetFloat("health", 0.85f);
UPSSaves.Prefs.SetString("playerName", "Hero");
UPSSaves.Prefs.SetBool("hardMode", true);

int    level    = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetInt("level",      defaultValue: 1);
float  health   = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetFloat("health",   defaultValue: 1f);
string player   = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetString("playerName", defaultValue: "Player");
bool   hardMode = UPSSaves.Prefs.GetBool("hardMode",  defaultValue: false);

docs.title: Flush to disk
docs.text:
UPSSaves.Prefs.TrySave();   // returns silently if IsReady == false

Info

You do not need to call this after every change - AutoSaver already handles periodic flushing. Use explicit saves only at important checkpoints, or if you implementing your own autosaves. Excessive save calls are discouraged, since platforms may have I/O limitations and save operations can be expensive.

docs.title: AutoSaver
docs.text:
A small interval timer used internally by UPSPlayerPrefs to flush periodically. The defaults are pulled from SavesSettings:

Setting Default Effect EnableAutosaves true Master switch SecondsBetweenAutosaves 300 Interval between auto-flushes

The AutoSaver is Tick-driven (Tick(Time.unscaledDeltaTime)), so it dont cooperates with paused / slowed game time.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Some console platforms require runtime error handling. The global dispatcher receives all errors raised through ErrorHandler.RaiseError(string), allowing the platform layer or game code to display the appropriate message (see Samples → Saves).

ErrorHandler.OnError += msg => CrashReporter.Send(msg);

docs.title: Saver - lower-level saves
docs.text:
Danger

Saver is considered an advanced API surface. Most projects should interact with the save system exclusively through UPSPlayerPrefs. This API is currently under development, may change in future versions, and is not yet as thoroughly tested as the main UPSPlayerPrefs workflow.

Use UPSSaves.Saver directly only when you need control beyond the key/value API: enumerating multiple named save files, writing a "named slot" save, or hooking the granular lifecycle events. Before using this API, wait for platform to finish initialization. You can check UPSSaves.IsReady to know when the system is ready to use.

docs.title: Writing a named save
docs.text:
void SetSaveData(string key, string data) => UPSSaves.Saver.CurrentSaveData[key] = data;
UPSSaves.Saver.Save();                          // auto-named: Save_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss
UPSSaves.Saver.Save("Slot1");                   // named slot

docs.title: Reading a named save
docs.text:
UPSSaves.Saver.OnLoadCompleted += success => Debug.Log($"Load: {success}");
UPSSaves.Saver.Load("Slot1");

Info

Load() is asynchronous because many platforms may perform save operations through cloud storage or other asynchronous I/O systems. Subscribe to OnLoadCompleted(bool) to know when the in-memory state has been replaced with the loaded data.

docs.title: Enumerating saves
docs.text:
UPSSaves.Saver.OnSavesFound += entries =>
{
    foreach (FileEntry e in entries)
        Debug.Log($"{e.Name}");
};
UPSSaves.Saver.StartSavesSearch();

docs.title: Live state
docs.text: CurrentSaveState is the in-memory Dictionary<string,string> that backs every UPSPlayerPrefs.Get*/Set* call. You normally don't poke it directly, but it can be useful for diagnostics.

docs.title: Lifecycle events
docs.text:
Saver implements ISaverEvents. Subscribe to whichever ones you need:

Event Fires OnSaveStarted(Dictionary<string,string>) About to write OnSaveCompleted(string) Write finished OnLoadStarted() About to read OnLoadCompleted(bool) Read finished OnSavesFound(FileEntry[]) Save directory enumeration finished OnReadError(int code, string message) Read failed (platform-specific code) OnWriteError(int code, string message) Write failed (platform-specific code)

docs.text:

docs.title: Platform abstraction
docs.text:
Warning

This section is still under development and may change in future SDK versions.

The Saves module itself is platform-free - there are no #if UNITY_GAMECORE blocks in Core/Saves. The seam is IFileSystem, supplied by whichever Platform subclass is active:

Platform IFileSystem implementation Desktop DesktopFileSystem (System.IO) Xbox (Series / One) XboxFileSystem (XGameSave API) PS4 PS4FileSystem PS5 PS5FileSystem Switch SwitchFileSystem

You normally never touch these directly. If you need to mock saves for a test harness or pipe them to a custom backend (e.g. cloud), implement IFileSystem and return it from a custom Platform.ProvideFileSystem() override.

docs.title: UI
docs.text: The UI module is a controller-friendly menu navigation system. Each screen is a Layer, layers contain UIElements (buttons, sliders, ...) and a Navigation graph that defines which element is reached by pressing up/down/left/right on the gamepad. Only one Layer is active at a time, and switching between them is a single static call. The module is intentionally lightweight since it does not draw anything, animate anything, or own a UI prefab. You build your panels with regular Unity UGUI components and the module wires up gamepad focus and directional traversal on top.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Layer-based screens - one active layer at a time.
  • Directional navigation graph - author per-element transitions for N / S / E / W
  • Gamepad friendly - driven by InputActionDefinition assets, glyph-aware out of the box
  • Component-based authoring - drop a Layer on a panel, LayerNavigator, LayerNavigation next to it.
  • Built-in element types - ActionButtonElement/ ActionSliderElement
  • Pre-built input definitions - UiButtonApply, UiButtonCancel, UiSlider, UiLayerNavigation shipped as assets
  • No bespoke prefabs - works with Canvas / RectTransform layout you already have

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Term What it is Layer MonoBehaviour attached to a your root. Has a unique Key. Self-registers with UILayersManager. LayerNavigator MonoBehaviour that reads directional input each frame and moves focus between elements LayerNavigation MonoBehaviour that holds the navigation graph: a default element + array of Transition Transition Serializable record: an origin UIElement and its North / South / West / East neighbours UIElement Abstract base for items. Tracks IsInFocus, IsEnabled, and the parent Layer ActionButtonElement UIElement for work with UGUI Button ActionSliderElement UIElement for work with UGUI Slider UILayersManager Static manager that tracks all registered layers and exposes ActivateLayer(...) ActivateLayerTrigger Helper component to activate a layer automatically on a Unity lifecycle hook

Info

There is no UI stack or history in this module - ActivateLayer(X) simply deactivates the previously active layer and activates X. If you need a back-stack, maintain it in your own code on top of UILayersManager.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Build a main menu with two buttons and one slider:

  1. Create the panel. Make a Canvas → Panel with two Button children (Play, Quit) and one Slider child (Volume).
  2. Add the Layer component to the panel root and set Key = "MainMenu".
  3. Add a default UiElement componnent to each Button/Slider:
    • On each button child, add ActionButtonElement and drop the shipped UiButtonApply definition into its bool-action slot. Also assign your button.
    • On the slider child, add ActionSliderElement and drop UiSlider definition into its Vector2 slot. Also assign your slider.
    • On each slider/button Assign a Layer wich you create before.
  4. Add LayerNavigation to the panel root. Set the Default Element to the Play button.
  5. Author transitions on LayerNavigation: each entry has an Origin element and one neighbour per direction. E.g. (Origin: Play, South: Quit). Add 3 transitions (Play, Quit, Volume origins)
  6. Add the LayerNavigator component next to LayerNavigation. Assign the shipped UiLayerNavigation definition asset to its input definition slot. Assign a Layer and LayerNavigation wich you create before
  7. Activate the layer at runtime Drop an ActivateLayerTrigger to the panel root with TriggerType = Start. Next, assing the target Layer using either a direct reference or its unique string key.
  8. Add any visual feedback UI feedback helps players clearly identify which element currently has focus (via sounds, particles, outlines, or color changes). For this test setup, we will use a simple color swap. Add the UIElementFeedback script to your ui elements, and assign the target Graphic in the Inspector:
    • For Buttons: Assign the child Text.
    • For Slider: Assign the Handle graphic.
public class UIElementFeedback : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private Graphic graphic;
    private Color highlightColor = Color.orange;

    private Color originalColor;
    private UIElement uiElement;

    private void Awake()
    {
        uiElement = GetComponent<UIElement>();
        originalColor = graphic.color;
    }

    private void OnEnable() => uiElement.OnFocusChanged += OnFocusChanged;
    private void OnDisable() => uiElement.OnFocusChanged -= OnFocusChanged;
    private void OnFocusChanged(bool oldValue, bool newValue) => graphic.color = newValue ? highlightColor : originalColor;
}

docs.title: Authoring a Layer
docs.text: The core components below sit on the root and make it a functional UI layer.

docs.title: Layer
docs.text:
Add the Layer component to the view root and give it a unique Key in the Inspector. That is all that's required - the component registers itself with UILayersManager as soon as the scene starts and removes itself when the GameObject is destroyed, so you never wire it up by hand.

Field What it does Key Unique string used by UILayersManager.ActivateLayer("...") lookups IsEnabled Read-only current state - flipped by activation, not by you

If you need to toggle a layer from script (without going through UILayersManager), call SetEnabled(bool) on the Layer reference.

docs.title: LayerNavigator
docs.text:
Add the LayerNavigator component next to the view root. It reads directional input each frame and moves focus between the elements declared in LayerNavigation.

In the Inspector:

  • Drop a Vector2ActionDefinition into its input slot (the shipped UiLayerNavigation.asset works out of the box).
  • Assign the Layer and the LayerNavigation references.

The first time the layer activates, the navigator focuses the default element from LayerNavigation automatically - you do not need to focus anything in code.

Event Fires OnSelectElement(UIElement prev, UIElement next) Focus moved from prev to next

docs.title: LayerNavigation
docs.text:
LayerNavigation defines how focus moves between UI elements when the player presses a navigation input (Up, Down, Left, Right) via LayerNavigator. This component holds an array of Transition and a default focus element. Empty slots mean "no neighbour in that direction" - input in that direction is ignored. You configure the graph directly in the Inspector:

Transition Origin North South West East Transition 1 Play ─ Quit ─ ─ Transition 2 Quit Play Volume ─ ─ Transition 3 Volume Quit ─ ─ ─

Info

If no default element is assigned, LayerNavigation automatically uses the first transition origin as the default element.

Code-based alternatives, this is especially useful for procedurally generated menus or dynamic UI layouts:

navigation.SetDefaultElement(playButton);
navigation.SetTransitions(new[] {
    new Transition(
        origin: playButton, 
        north: null,        
        south: quitElement,   
        west: null, 
        east: null),

    new Transition(
        origin: quitElement,       
        north: playButton,  
        south: volumeElement, 
        west: null, 
        east: null),

    new Transition(
        origin: volumeElement,     
        north: quitElement, 
        south: null,          
        west: null, 
        east: null),
});

docs.title: Activating layers
docs.text:
When Layer is wired up you need to actually switch to it at runtime. There are two ways.

From code, via UILayersManager:

UILayersManager.ActivateLayer("MainMenu");          // by key
UILayersManager.ActivateLayer(settingsLayer);       // by reference

Layer current = UILayersManager.CurrentActiveLayer; // currently active layer (or null)

ActivateLayer deactivates whatever layer was previously active and activates the new one. There is no stack, so calling it again with the same key is a no-op.

Declaratively, via ActivateLayerTrigger:

For the common cases - "activate this layer on Start", "switch to Settings when the Settings button is clicked" - drop an ActivateLayerTrigger component instead of writing code.

Field Values TriggerType Awake, Start, OnEnable, OnDisable, OnDestroy, Manual FindType Key (resolve the target Layer by its Key string) or Reference (direct slot)

With TriggerType = Manual, fire it from code or button OnClick event:

settingsTrigger.ExecuteTrigger();

docs.title: UI Elements
docs.text: The components that live on the focusable items inside a layer (buttons, sliders, and your own subclasses).

docs.title: UIElement (base)
docs.text:
UIElement is the abstract base class for any focusable item in a layer. It tracks focus / enabled state, exposes the events you'll use to wire up visual feedback, and provides one extension point (Interact()) for subclasses.

Member Kind What it does IsInFocus property True when the navigator currently has focus on this element IsEnabled property True when the element is interactable Layer property The parent layer this element belongs to SetFocus method Programmatically focus / unfocus SetEnabled method Programmatically enable / disable Event Fires OnInteracted Subclass called Interact() - e.g. button clicked OnFocusChanged(bool old, bool current) Focus state changed OnEnabledChanged(bool old, bool current) Enabled state changed

You can subclass UIElement for custom element types - the UIElementFeedback snippet in Quick start is a minimal example that uses OnFocusChanged to drive a colour swap.

docs.title: ActionButtonElement
docs.text:
Works with default UGUI Button. Listens to a BoolActionDefinition (usually UiButtonApply) and invokes the button's onClick when that input performs. Optionally renders the controller glyph for the bound input using the active GamepadIconsSet from UpscaleSDKConfig.

Inspector field Type Notes Action definition BoolActionDefinition Usually the shipped UiButtonApply asset Button UnityEngine.UI.Button Target UGUI button on the same GameObject Layer Layer Parent layer reference

docs.title: ActionSliderElement
docs.text:
Works with default UGUI Slider. Reads a Vector2ActionDefinition (usually UiSlider) and nudges the slider by the configured step per direction tick.

Inspector field Type Notes Action definition Vector2ActionDefinition Usually the shipped UiSlider asset Slider UnityEngine.UI.Slider Target UGUI slider on the same GameObject Step amount float How much to nudge per tick of input Layer Layer Parent layer reference

docs.title: Input integration
docs.text:
The UI module does not talk to BaseInputActionSet directly. Instead, every input-driven component holds an InputActionDefinition<T> slot - the ScriptableObject authoring surface described in Manual → Input → Action Definitions.

Component Definition type Shipped default asset LayerNavigator Vector2ActionDefinition UiLayerNavigation.asset ActionButtonElement BoolActionDefinition (Apply) UiButtonApply.asset ActionButtonElement BoolActionDefinition (Cancel) UiButtonCancel.asset ActionButtonElement BoolActionDefinition (Base) UiButtonBase.asset ActionButtonElement BoolActionDefinition (Extra) UiButtonExtra.asset ActionSliderElement Vector2ActionDefinition UiSlider.asset

All defaults live at Assets/UpscaleSDK/Core/UI/Runtime/DefaultDefinitions/.

docs.text:
The shared baseline applies to every platform:

docs.text: Platform-specific layer for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Provides save-data I/O through IFileSystem using standard System.IO.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Hands-on examples shipped under Assets/UpscaleSDK/Samples. Each sample is a self-contained scene you can copy into your project as a starting point.

  • Input — gamepad live tester and per-platform controller glyph prefabs
  • Saves — read / write int / float / string / bool, with an error-popup hook
  • UI — controller-friendly menu navigation: layers, transitions, focus feedback

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Two scenes that exercise the Input module: one is a live tester of gamepad input via BaseInputActionSet, the other is a set of drop-in prefabs that render the correct controller glyph for each input shape.

docs.title: Gamepad
docs.text:
A visual tester that lights up gamepad input - sticks, triggers, face buttons, D-pad, shoulders. Useful for sanity-checking a new device, validating that an IInputProvider swap still reads everything, or just confirming BaseInputActionSet is wired up after a fresh install.

Scene Assets/UpscaleSDK/Samples/Input/Gamepad/Gamepad.unity Script GamepadDemo.cs

docs.title: What it demonstrates
docs.text:
• Polling BaseInputActionSet every frame with .Read() - no events, no subscriptions
  • Reading every category of input the set exposes (bool buttons, float triggers, Vector2 sticks / D-pad)
  • Mapping a raw input value to a UI response (color swap for buttons / triggers)

Info

Note the use of .Hold on ButtonActionGroup for the buttons - that's the variant that returns true for every frame the button is held, which is exactly what you want for a "lights up while pressed" indicator. See Manual → Input → Button triggers for the difference between Press, Hold, and Release.

docs.title: Glyphs
docs.text:
A scene of small reusable components that each render the correct controller glyph for one kind of input - a button, an action, a 1D axis (trigger), or a 2D axis (stick).

Scene Assets/UpscaleSDK/Samples/Input/Glyphs/Gamepad/GamepadGlyphs.unity Scripts GlyphForGamepadButton.cs, GlyphForGamepadAction.cs, GlyphForGamepad1DAxis.cs, GlyphForGamepad2DAxis.cs Prefabs GlyphForGamepadButton.prefab, GlyphForGamepadAction.prefab, GlyphForGamepad1dAxis.prefab, GlyphForGamepad2dAxis.prefab

docs.title: What it demonstrates
docs.text:
• Resolving a GamepadGlyph sprite at runtime via the active GamepadIconsSet on UpscaleSDKConfig
  • Basic usage of TryGetGlyph in InputAction<T>.

Tip

In most cases, you can use Action Definitions from Manual → Input → Action Definitions to resolve sprites.

Warning

Make sure your UpscaleSDKConfig has the per-platform GamepadIconsSet references filled in (see Manual → Input → Glyphs).

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
An demonstration of UPSPlayerPrefs: a grid of focusable elements, each bound to a different key/type (int, float, string, bool). Press Apply to mutate the value at the focused cell, watch the on-screen text refresh, then quit and re-open the scene - the values persist through the configured IFileSystem.

Scene Assets/UpscaleSDK/Samples/Saves/Saves.unity Scripts SavesTest.cs, ErrorPopup.cs, PopupErrorHandler.cs Prefab ErrorPopupPrefab.prefab

docs.title: What it demonstrates
docs.text:
• The full UPSPlayerPrefs surface - GetInt / SetInt, GetFloat / SetFloat, GetString / SetString, GetBool / SetBool
  • Gating reads / writes on UPSSaves.Prefs.IsReady
  • Driving a UI element from a UIElement's OnFocusChanged / OnInteracted events
  • Wiring an in-game popup to ErrorHandler.OnError so save failures actually surface to the player

docs.title: How to run
docs.text:
1. Open Saves.unity.
  2. Press Play. The grid loads its current values from storage (defaults if first launch).
  3. Navigate with the gamepad / arrows and press the Apply button - the focused cell mutates its key.
  4. Stop and re-enter Play. The mutated values are still there.

Info

This scene wires PopupErrorHandler to ErrorHandler.OnError so any I/O failure raised through the global dispatcher spawns the ErrorPopupPrefab with the message attached.

Warning

Make sure you complete a saves module setup. (see Manual → Saves → Setup).

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
The reference scene for the UI module - a menu wired up with usage of core components Layer, LayerNavigator, LayerNavigation, ActionButtonElement, and ActionSliderElement. It covers the common patterns you'll repeat across your own menus: directional navigation across a grid, a focus-driven feedback hook, and opening / closing panels.

Scene Assets/UpscaleSDK/Samples/UI/Base/UIExampleScene.unity Scripts DemoWindow.cs, DynamicGridDemo.cs, UIFeedbackDemo.cs

docs.title: What it demonstrates
docs.text:
• A Layer + LayerNavigator + LayerNavigation panel built from regular UGUI components
  • Two-axis navigation through a grid (DynamicGridDemo) - LayerNavigation transitions wired horizontally and vertically
  • Reacting to focus changes with UIElement.OnFocusChanged to drive visual feedback (UIFeedbackDemo)
  • A simple panel open/close pattern with DemoWindow.Open() / DemoWindow.Close()

docs.title: How to run
docs.text:
1. Open UIExampleScene.unity.
  2. Press Play.
  3. Use the gamepad's left stick / D-pad to move between elements. Apply on the focused element interacts with it; Cancel closes a sub-panel.

Warning

Make sure your UpscaleSDKConfig has the per-platform GamepadIconsSet references filled in (see Manual → Input → Glyphs).
